source.title: Random CNN structure: tool to increase generalization ability in deep learning
source.authors: B. Świderski; S. Osowski; Grzegorz Gwardys; J. Kurek; M. Słowińska; Iwona Lugowska

record.tranche_reason: The study compares random selection of activation functions with fixed-activation CNNs and reports test-set metrics; this conceptually tests whether a training/architecture condition changes generalization.
record.gate_note: Tests random activation-structure selection on natural dermoscopic labels. It does not test random-label memorization or the other claim versions. Figures 4–5 describe trends but do not provide extractable numeric series; table values are reported separately.
record.test_reason: The study tests random activation-path selection against fixed-activation CNNs, which none of V1–V8 names. Natural-label test accuracy alone does not test V1; using Adam and a fixed batch size does not test V4 or V5. Training-data score margins do not test magnitude-aware sharpness in V7. Original sources are cited as background.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase captures the authors' interpretation: random selection between parameterized ReLU and softplus sublayers improves generalization on a small dermoscopic dataset and acts as implicit regularization. Describe the actual classes as verruca seborrhoica and basal cell carcinoma; the paper calls these non-melanoma and melanoma. Its conclusion overstates uniform metric improvements: Table 1 shows lower specificity and precision than ReLU, and no significance test is reported.
record.recipe_differences: Randomly selects between parallel ReLU and softplus sublayers; compares with fixed-activation CNNs. Uses a small medical image dataset and reports test-set metrics, without testing the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation structure changes the reported test metrics; the authors report softplus is especially sensitive to prolonged training and describe overlearning in its test-accuracy curve.

fits_no_version.finding: Random CNN achieved mean accuracy of 91.8%, versus 91.4% for ReLU and 89.9% for softplus, on 213 dermoscopic images. Its mean AUC was also higher. These are comparisons of the authors' proposed method.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random selection between ReLU and softplus parameterized sublayers can improve held-out classification metrics on this small dermoscopic dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean training-data score margins were 0.836 for random CNN, 0.830 for ReLU, and 0.800 for softplus.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random activation-path selection can increase mean training-data score margin relative to fixed activations in this experiment.

record.peer_reviewed: EURASIP Journal on Image and Video Processing
record.problems: The study uses only 213 images from a single medical classification task. Test metrics are reported, but paired training errors and train-test gaps are not. The authors describe results as tenfold cross-validation averages and provide standard deviations; Figures 4–5 show epoch trends without numeric series in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported numeric results were omitted. Figures 4–5 are described in text but provide no extractable numeric series, so no figure-only rows were added.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the coexistence of memorization capacity with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with other complexity measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The original tests classification performance, not any listed version. Figure 4's final smoothed accuracies describe a particular run and should not replace Table 1's repeated-experiment averages. Figure-only trends are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Widening past interpolation and test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and tuning.
Dropout and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removing influential memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
